requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
The sources satisfy the requirement. I checked each obligation against the {impl} code and the tests, and I found no gaps. I did not read the per-language profile code that builds outline nodes for Markdown, TOML, YAML and Rust.

**Implementation**
- **Path and root.** `parse_selector` returns no segments for the empty selector. `Outline::resolve` (`src/outline/mod.rs`) starts at the root and walks children by segment, so the empty selector selects the root. `split_segments` splits on `/` outside brackets.
- **Named segments.** `Segment::base` writes `kind[name]`, using `encode_name` on each name part. The `/` that joins the two parts of a trait-impl name sits inside the brackets. That is a separate requirement's convention, not a violation here.
- **Anonymous segments.** `Builder::finish` builds `kind@hash` from the first `HASH_DIGITS` (12) hex digits of the node's identity hash. `plain_text` does the same for `line` nodes, whose identity hash is the line hash.
- **Disambiguation.** `disambiguate` groups siblings by identical base segment and appends `#N`, the one-based source-order position, to every member of a group with more than one. It skips `line` nodes. `Outline::resolve` returns the first child whose segment matches, so a `line` selector resolves whenever a line with that content exists. `ParsedSource::resolve` in `src/inputs.rs` reports an ambiguous selector, one that needs a `#N`, separately from one that matches nothing.
- **Percent-encoding.** `encode_name` encodes `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and any whitespace as uppercase UTF-8 byte escapes. `decode_name` reverses this. It rejects malformed escapes, unescaped delimiters, unescaped whitespace and non-UTF-8 results.
- **No line numbers.** Selectors are built only from kind, name or hash, and ordinal. Line numbers are stored on `OutlineNode` but never enter a segment or selector.
- **Marking.** All the selector code is marked `{impl}`: the selector types, errors and parsing in `selector.rs`, plus `disambiguate`, `finish`, `plain_text`, `root_node` and `resolve` in `mod.rs`. I found no unmarked code implementing the requirement.

**Minor leniency.** `decode_name` uses `u8::from_str_radix`, which accepts a leading `+`, so `%+1` would decode. This does not break the requirement's round-trip guarantee.

**Tests**
- `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` checks the exact encoding of a name containing space, `/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@`, `%`, a tab and a non-ASCII character. It also checks round-trip decoding and rejection of bad input.
- `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` checks the empty selector, two-part names, `#N`, a 12-digit hash, and a list of invalid forms.
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` covers many node kinds, nested paths, percent-encoded names, `#1`/`#2` disambiguation, resolving the empty selector to the root, and errors for an ambiguous or missing selector.
- `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` checks that anonymous selectors survive inserting an unrelated item and break when the item itself changes. It also checks `#N` for duplicate anonymous nodes.
- `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` checks that duplicate lines get identical selectors without `#N`, that such a selector resolves, and that the word rule applies, so `two  words` equals `two words` but differs from `twowords`.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile
MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text MUST be hashed,
not its delimiter tokens such as `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`,
so reflowing it across more or fewer lines does not change the hash. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
